name: Algorithmic Trading Strategy Backtest
description: strategy_code (Python) defines a class Strategy with a no-argument constructor and a method decide(price_history, portfolio) that the harness calls exactly once per bar of a harness-generated, curator-seeded synthetic price path -- NEVER receiving any bar beyond today's, by construction (see strategy_code's own help text). The harness owns the entire walk-forward event loop: it generates the price path itself from market_params' own pinned Geometric Brownian Motion formula, drives strategy_code bar-by-bar in a SEPARATE OS process that never receives future prices, builds the real resulting equity curve itself from real portfolio state after every bar, and independently computes Sharpe ratio / Sortino ratio / max drawdown / CAGR / Calmar ratio from that real curve using the harness's own from-scratch formula implementation (see harness.js's own module doc comment for the exact pinned formulas) -- never trusting any number strategy_code itself might compute or print. This is run against EVERY seed market_params declares (at least 2 independent seeds required, mechanically enforced) so a curator cannot author a row against a single lucky/tuned price path; the curator's own expected_metrics must match what the harness independently computes for EVERY seed, within a curator-declared tolerance. A row whose real performance is implausibly good on EVERY seed simultaneously (a red flag on what is, by construction, a random walk with no genuine exploitable edge) is rejected outright as a likely lookahead/measurement bug rather than silently accepted. This category is coding-domain, not finance-domain: the subject matter is trading-strategy CODE, execution-verified exactly like every other category in this registry, not a financial-advice or real-market-data category (the sandbox has no network egress, so real historical market data is never used or needed).
executionEnv: python3 (stdlib only: random, math, statistics, json, subprocess, sys, os -- no numpy, no pandas, no third-party packages of any kind). The harness spawns TWO real, separate python3 OS processes per row: a 'driver' process (generates the seeded price path(s) and drives the bar-by-bar loop) and a 'runner' process (loads strategy_code exactly once and calls its decide() method once per bar) -- see harness.js's own module doc comment for why this is a real security boundary, not an implementation convenience.

fields.label: Task description
fields.help: Natural-language description of the trading strategy CONCEPT being implemented, e.g. 'a simple moving-average crossover strategy: go fully invested when a fast moving average crosses above a slow one, move to cash when it crosses back below' or 'a mean-reversion strategy that buys after a sharp short-term drop and sells after a sharp short-term rally'. This is flavor/framing text for a human/LLM audit stage, read by whoever writes strategy_code to decide what logic to implement -- it is NOT the mechanically-checked contract. The harness never parses this field at all; its own pass/fail decision is driven entirely by strategy_code's own REAL, OBSERVED behavior against market_params' own REAL synthetic price path(s), cross-checked against expected_metrics (see that field's own help text). Unlike retry_backoff_resilience's strategy_description (which must restate exact numbers a reference state-machine can independently verify), a trading strategy's own logic is open-ended and arbitrary -- there is no finite, enumerable set of 'correct' strategies this harness could check against, the same reasoning numerical_precision's own module doc comment already documents for arbitrary curator-authored formulas. Ground truth for THIS row is instead expected_metrics, curator-authored by actually running strategy_code for real (see that field's own help text) -- the same trust model numerical_precision already uses, applied here to strategy PERFORMANCE rather than a single scalar output.

fields.label: Market parameters (curator-authored ground truth, JSON)
fields.help: Curator-authored, fixed context (never graded, never written by the contributor, never sent into strategy_code's own Python process at all -- strategy_code only ever sees the resulting PRICES, one bar at a time, never these parameters). A JSON object: {"seeds": [int, int, ...] (2-5 distinct integers, each 0 <= seed <= 2147483647 -- at least 2 REQUIRED, mechanically enforced: this is the category's primary anti-overfitting/anti-hardcoding mechanism, since strategy_code must be re-run against EVERY declared seed's own independently-generated price path and its real performance on EACH must match this row's own expected_metrics -- a strategy curve-fit to exploit one specific price sequence has no mechanism to also 'fake' correct-looking performance on a genuinely different, independently-drawn random path), "drift": number (-0.01 to 0.01, the expected per-BAR log-drift), "volatility": number (0 < v <= 0.05, the per-BAR log-return standard deviation), "num_bars": integer (50-500, the number of GENERATED bars after the initial price), "initial_price": number (0 < p <= 1000000)}. EXACT PINNED PRICE-PATH FORMULA (Geometric Brownian Motion, the standard, textbook-documented model for a synthetic asset price with no real exploitable edge -- chosen over a plain arithmetic random walk because GBM guarantees the price stays strictly positive for every finite draw, which this category's own long-only [0,1] position-sizing contract relies on -- see strategy_code's own help text): the resulting series has num_bars+1 points, price[0] = initial_price; for i = 1..num_bars, price[i] = price[i-1] * exp((drift - 0.5*volatility^2) + volatility*Z_i), where Z_i is drawn from Python's OWN stdlib `random.gauss(0.0, 1.0)`, called EXACTLY num_bars times in order (i=1..num_bars), immediately after seeding that SAME seed via `random.seed(seed)` once at the very start of this seed's own path generation and nothing else drawing from the `random` module in between. AUTHORING GUIDANCE -- reproduce this EXACT path locally with plain Python stdlib (no numpy needed) before authoring expected_metrics: `import random, math; random.seed(SEED); prices = [INITIAL_PRICE]; [prices.append(prices[-1] * math.exp((DRIFT - 0.5*VOLATILITY**2) + VOLATILITY*random.gauss(0.0, 1.0))) for _ in range(NUM_BARS)]`. Prefer num_bars >= 100 for a less noise-dominated backtest (a 50-bar backtest annualizes very short-run luck into large Sharpe/CAGR swings -- still mechanically allowed, but a curator authoring one should expect noisier, less discriminating metrics). Prefer realistic equity-like magnitudes (drift ~0.0002-0.0008/bar, volatility ~0.005-0.02/bar) unless deliberately authoring an edge-case row -- see expected_metrics' own help text for the implausible-performance sanity gate this triggers if violated.

fields.label: Trading strategy implementation (Python)
fields.help: THE GRADED ARTIFACT. Python code defining EXACTLY ONE top-level class named `Strategy`, with a no-argument constructor (`def __init__(self):` -- hardcode this row's own strategy logic/parameters here, reading task_description's prose; the harness never passes market_params in, so there is nothing here to blindly echo) and EXACTLY this method: `def decide(self, price_history, portfolio):`. The harness calls decide() ONCE PER BAR, in order, for every bar of every seed's own price path: `price_history` is a plain Python list of floats, `price_history[-1]` is TODAY's price (the current bar being decided), `price_history[0]` is the very first observed price, and its length grows by exactly one every call -- it is a FRESH list object every call (never the same list mutated later), and it PHYSICALLY CANNOT contain any future bar: the harness's own bar-by-bar event loop simply never constructs, let alone transmits, any price beyond the current one until the corresponding later call actually happens (see harness.js's own module doc comment for the real, two-OS-process architecture that makes this a genuine security boundary, not just an API convention a determined submission could bypass via a global variable or stack-frame introspection). `portfolio` is a plain dict `{"cash": float, "position": float, "equity": float}` describing the REAL portfolio state immediately BEFORE today's trade is applied (position is share count, always >= 0; equity = cash + position*price_history[-1]). decide() must return a single float in the CLOSED range [0.0, 1.0] -- interpreted as the TARGET FRACTION of total equity to hold in the asset immediately after today's trade (0.0 = fully cash, 1.0 = fully invested; this category is long-only with no leverage and no shorting -- a returned value outside [0.0, 1.0], or of any type other than a real number [booleans are explicitly rejected, since Python's bool is a bool-flavored int], is a hard failure for that row, not clamped). The harness rebalances the portfolio to exactly this target every single bar (a strategy that wants to 'hold' must keep returning the SAME target_weight every bar -- since the underlying position's OWN value already moves with the price, returning a constant weight causes zero unnecessary rebalancing trades by construction; this is the same target-percent semantics real backtesting frameworks use). Trading is frictionless (no commission, no slippage, no bid/ask spread) -- a deliberate simplification kept out of this category's first version, documented here rather than silently assumed; INITIAL_CAPITAL is a fixed harness constant, 100000.0, identical for every row and every seed. NOTHING else about market_params (drift, volatility, seed, num_bars) is ever visible to this code -- decide() must infer everything it needs from price_history and portfolio alone, exactly the same 'read the prose, never receive the ground-truth parameters' contract already established by retry_backoff_resilience's retry_call/rate_limiting_policy_simulation's RateLimiter.check.

fields.label: Expected backtest metrics (curator-computed ground truth, JSON)
fields.help: JSON object `{"tolerance": {"sharpe": n, "sortino": n, "max_drawdown": n, "cagr": n, "calmar": n}, "per_seed": [{"seed": s, "sharpe": n, "sortino": n, "max_drawdown": n, "cagr": n, "calmar": n}, ...]}`, hand-computed by the curator by ACTUALLY RUNNING this row's own strategy_code against EVERY seed market_params declares (never guessed, never estimated, never copied from a similar row -- the same 'curator must genuinely verify their own row' discipline numerical_precision and retry_backoff_resilience already established, load-bearing here because this category has NO way to independently derive what a genuinely novel strategy's own performance SHOULD be the way rate_limiting_policy_simulation/caching_strategy can independently derive a fixed algorithm's decisions). `per_seed` must contain EXACTLY one entry per seed in market_params.seeds (matched by the `seed` value itself, not by array position) -- a missing seed, a duplicate, or a seed value not present in market_params.seeds is a dataset-authoring defect, rejected before strategy_code is ever run. Each entry's five metric values are independently recomputed by the harness from strategy_code's own REAL equity curve on that REAL seed's own price path (never trusted from this field directly) using these EXACT pinned formulas -- see harness.js's own module doc comment for the full derivation and rationale for each choice: per-bar simple returns r_i = (equity_i - equity_{i-1}) / equity_{i-1} for i=1..num_bars; `sharpe` = (mean(r) / stdev(r)) * sqrt(252) using the SAMPLE standard deviation (Python's statistics.stdev, divisor n-1), 0.0 if stdev(r) is exactly 0; `sortino` = (mean(r) / downside_deviation) * sqrt(252) where downside_deviation = sqrt(mean(min(r_i, 0)^2)) over ALL bars (the 'full' downside-deviation convention, minimum acceptable return = 0), 0.0 if downside_deviation is exactly 0; `max_drawdown` = the most negative value of (equity_i - running_peak_i) / running_peak_i across the WHOLE curve including bar 0 (a non-positive number; 0.0 means the curve never fell below its own running peak); `cagr` = (equity_final / equity_initial)^(252/num_bars) - 1 (252 = the fixed trading-days-per-year annualization constant this category uses uniformly -- pin this exact value when hand-computing, never a different one); `calmar` = cagr / abs(max_drawdown), 0.0 if max_drawdown is exactly 0.0. `tolerance` declares the ABSOLUTE tolerance for each of the five metrics, applied identically across every seed -- since these are the SAME deterministic formulas applied to a byte-reproducible price path (see market_params' own help text), values should be exactly or near-exactly reproducible: a small tolerance (0.01-0.05 for sharpe/sortino/cagr/max_drawdown; up to 0.1-0.5 for calmar, which amplifies small max_drawdown differences) accommodating only minor cross-machine floating-point ordering differences is expected, never curator arithmetic slack. IMPLAUSIBLE-PERFORMANCE SANITY GATE: since market_params' own price path is a pure random walk with no genuine embedded edge (see that field's own help text), the harness independently rejects any row whose REAL computed sharpe ratio exceeds 5.0 on EVERY declared seed SIMULTANEOUSLY -- a threshold chosen because even top-tier real-world quantitative strategies rarely sustain an annualized Sharpe above 3-4 over any meaningful sample, so consistently exceeding 5.0 across multiple independently-seeded random walks is a strong, if not mathematically certain, signal of a lookahead bug or an equity-accounting defect rather than genuine skill (documented as a heuristic threshold, not a proof, the same tier as this registry's other documented heuristic gates -- see retry_backoff_resilience's checkSuspectedMissingJitter for the precedent). Requiring ALL seeds to trip it (not just one) avoids false-rejecting a strategy that simply got a lucky single draw.
